AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Virtual reality (VR) simulators have become useful tools in various fields of medicine. Prominent uses of VR technologies include assessment of physician skills and for pre-surgical planning. VR has demonstrated effectiveness in multiple surgical specialties, yet its use in the field of neurosurgery remains limited to date.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To examine all current literature on VR based simulation for pre-surgical planning and training in cranial tumor surgeries and to assess the quality of these studies.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: PubMed and Embase where systematically searched to identify studies that utilized VR for pre-surgical planning and/or studies that investigated the use of VR as a training tool from inception to May 25, 2017.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The initial search identified 1662 articles. Thirty-seven full-text articles were assessed for inclusion. Nine studies were ultimately included. These were subdivided into pre-surgical planning and training using VR.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Prospects for VR are bright when surgical planning and skills training are considered. In terms of surgical planning, VR has noted and documented utility in the planning of cranial surgeries. Further, VR has been central to establishing reproducible benchmarks of performance in relation to cranial tumor resection which are helpful not only in demonstrating face and construct validity but also in enhancing neurosurgical training in a way not previously examined. While additional studies are needed to better delineate the precise role of VR in each of these capacities, these studies stand to demonstrate the utility of VR in the neurosurgery and highlight the need for further investigation.
